# Wind Tunnel — devlog

> A wind tunnel 1.3m long, and 0.4m in height and width at its longest ends, used for measuring wind resistance on different subway cart roofs.  Compares the drag force experienced by 5 different hypothetical cart roofs using a load sensor and miniature wind tunnel reaching relative speeds of 35 km/h, to find which one is most aerodynamic. Modelled the cart roofs using blender and simply changed the height increment of each, keeping the same curvature model. Made the intake and exhaust of the wind tunnel using double layered cardboard with plywood for the test section, held together using wood glue and tape. Wind speeds were increased using a 136 W Vevor Fan.  Load Cell was connect to a HX711 load cell amplifier module (which I soldered the pins and wires to)  which was then connected to an Arduino UNO and finally my laptop.  I coded the arduino to transform all electrical values into force measurements and find the average of 20 values (each gotten from an original 10  individual values averaged)  gathered over 20 seconds.

## Build

### 2026-10-01 — Cut out the cardboard for the intake and exhaust portions, glued them together with wood glue instead of hot glue, but took a while to let it dry. Picked up plywood and glued them together using wood

**4h**

Cut out the cardboard for the intake and exhaust portions, glued them together with wood glue instead of hot glue, but took a while to let it dry. Picked up plywood and glued them together using wood glue as well. Had an error using making the design so I had extra holes in the corner which the laser cutter removed completely instead of making incisions.

I used little “ribs” to help keep the bent pieces of cardboard still together.

Haven’t glued the sections together yet or taped up the tiny air gaps.

ALSO, why is my clear acrylic just NOT clear, like I wanted to be able to see through it but I just cant.
